turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Come on back. I'm Dr. Ellison. Lap or table, Leo, your call. What brings you in?

[SEG0002] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): His ear. He's four, nights have been awful with crying, and I'm pretty sure it's the right one after a cold. I have to tell you the cold or the ear won't make sense, and I know I over-explain, so stop me if you need to.
[SEG0003] person_1 (DOCTOR): I won't stop you yet.
[SEG0004] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): So the cold started two weeks—
[SEG0005] person_3 (PATIENT): I want a sticker.

[SEG0006] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): —ago? No, sorry, about ten days ago. Clear runny nose and a cough that was worse at night. The nose is mostly dried up, and the cough is still a little, mostly in the morning.
[SEG0007] person_1 (DOCTOR): When did the ear join in?

[SEG0008] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I almost said five days because I'm tired, but it's not. Friday night he woke up screaming, so three nights. He grabs the right ear and won't lay on that side, and daytime he's just cranky.
[SEG0009] person_3 (PATIENT): My ear doesn't hurt.
[SEG0010] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): You say that now.
[SEG0011] person_1 (DOCTOR): Daytime's different sometimes. Any fever with all this?
[SEG0012] person_3 (PATIENT): I dreamed about a big truck. It was loud.

[SEG0013] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No. I checked under the tongue, and he actually cooperates. It was ninety-eight point four yesterday and the same this morning. Grandma was over and she kept saying he felt hot, like she was completely sure.
[SEG0014] person_1 (DOCTOR): She thought it was a fever?
[SEG0015] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): She was sure. I wasn't, the thermometer didn't agree, so I'm saying no fever.
[SEG0016] person_3 (PATIENT): I was hot. Grandma said hot potato. My pajamas were hot and the blanket was scratchy and I kicked it off and I was still hot and I wanted water.
[SEG0017] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He'll give you a whole paragraph. He felt warm to her hand, but the number was normal. I still say no fever.
[SEG0018] person_1 (DOCTOR): Noted, both versions. Any drainage, like pus, from that ear?
[SEG0019] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No pus. I looked with a phone light, which is silly, but nothing was coming out.
[SEG0020] person_1 (DOCTOR): Hearing seem off at all?
[SEG0021] person_3 (PATIENT): The truck dream had a horn.
[SEG0022] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Oh, hearing, sorry, he jumped in. No, he hears the TV even when I turn it way down. I meant to answer you and then I lost the question.
[SEG0023] person_1 (DOCTOR): All good. With the cough, any trouble breathing or wheezing?
[SEG0024] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No wheezing, just that leftover morning cough. He wheezed one time as a baby with a different cold, not now.
[SEG0025] person_1 (DOCTOR): What have you used for the pain?

[SEG0026] person_3 (PATIENT): The pink medicine, strawberry but not a real strawberry, and I swallow it. I can tell you how the cup works, there's a line and Mommy says stop and one time I wanted to go past it. She said no, so I didn't, and then I asked why the line is there.

[SEG0027] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): That's the Tylenol, the children's red box, 160 milligrams in each 5 mL. I told my sister five mils and that was me misremembering, we fill the syringe to 7.5. Every six hours when he's crying, not around the clock, and it helps for maybe an hour. Sitting up on the couch is what really helps, and flat is worse.
[SEG0028] person_1 (DOCTOR): Anything else he's on, vitamins or drops?
[SEG0029] person_3 (PATIENT): There was another pink one when I was little at Grandma's, and she tells the story every single time and it goes on and on and I just wait for it to stop.

[SEG0030] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): That's not a medicine now. When he was about fifteen months they gave him amox— I keep calling it Augmentin and that's wrong, it was amoxicillin, the pink liquid. For an ear, I think, or maybe his throat, long ago. He finished the bottle, I think.
[SEG0031] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any reaction to that amoxicillin?

[SEG0032] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I think he got a rash, maybe, a couple days into it. It could've been the virus, I honestly don't know. My mother calls it an allergy, and I was never sure enough to put it on a form. So maybe don't write allergic in stone.
[SEG0033] person_1 (DOCTOR): Possible rash, not proven, so amoxicillin stays in the maybe column. Any foods or other drugs he can't have?
[SEG0034] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Not that I know of. No food stuff. I would remember hives.
[SEG0035] person_1 (DOCTOR): Leo, I'm going to look in your ears with a little light. It stays on the outside.

[SEG0036] person_3 (PATIENT): Last time the light was cold and I said ow, but it was surprise not hurt. They had a brown dog sticker, not a cat, because Mason's cat scratches. I started telling the lady the whole cat story and she said honey we have to keep moving.
[SEG0037] person_1 (DOCTOR): Sticker after this, I promise. Let me see the right ear.

[SEG0038] person_1 (DOCTOR): The right eardrum is a little pink, the landmarks are still there, and it's not bulging. No hole and nothing draining. The left ear looks normal. Throat is clear with no pus, and the neck glands aren't swollen.
[SEG0039] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): So is it infected? Don't soften it for me.

[SEG0040] person_1 (DOCTOR): I'm working it through out loud. A cold swells the little drainage tube, fluid sits there, and lying down makes it throb. This could be a mild ear infection, or just pressure and fluid without much infection. I can't cleanly separate those on one look.
[SEG0041] person_3 (PATIENT): Is there a bug in my ear?
[SEG0042] person_1 (DOCTOR): No bug, just irritation. His forehead isn't warm right now, but I didn't take a temperature in the room, so that's only my hand.

[SEG0043] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): A few other things while he's quiet. He mentioned his tummy yesterday, then ate two waffles, so forget the tummy, and he's drinking milk and juice fine with a slightly lower appetite. Home is just the two of us, and he does preschool mornings where half the class is coughing. They pass colds around like snacks.
[SEG0044] person_1 (DOCTOR): I don't need to march through every other system. Drinking is the piece I cared about, and we'll leave the tummy if you're leaving it.

[SEG0045] person_3 (PATIENT): I didn't sleep. I waked up and the drum was going boom boom in my ear and I cried and Mommy came and my bear fell and I couldn't find him in the dark. My ear was really really hurting, not pretend, and I wanted the pink medicine and the couch, not the bed.
[SEG0046] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Every night since Friday, so yes, the ear hurts, he just won't say it until he feels safe. Nights are the bad part and days he mostly plays.
[SEG0047] person_1 (DOCTOR): So worse when he's flat, better sitting up, and Tylenol only takes the edge off. Did he ever actually swallow ibuprofen, the brown one?

[SEG0048] person_3 (PATIENT): The brown one is spicy and I spit it at Grandma's. She made a face and started the long medicine story, and I stopped listening when she said rash because rash stories are boring. I wanted a cracker instead and she said after the story, which is never after.
[SEG0049] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): One try, and he spit the whole thing, so I don't count a dose he didn't swallow. We can try again if you really want, but I know how that goes.

[SEG0050] person_1 (DOCTOR): No need to fight him over it. Keep the Tylenol at 7.5 mL every six hours only when he needs it, and don't wake him just to dose. If he'll take it, children's ibuprofen is 5 mL, that's 100 milligrams, every eight hours with a snack. A warm cloth on the outside of the ear and keeping his head propped up can help too.
[SEG0051] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): What about an antibiotic? Grandma already texted me a name, and I'm not freelancing that.

[SEG0052] person_1 (DOCTOR): I wouldn't start one today. It's been three nights, there's no fever we can document, the drum isn't bulging, and he's drinking. Plenty of these settle in a couple of days with pain medicine, so this is watchful waiting.
[SEG0053] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): If they don't settle, I need the back-up plan before I leave, or I'll spin on it at ten p.m.

[SEG0054] person_1 (DOCTOR): I'll send a prescription today so it can sit at the pharmacy. Azithromycin suspension, 200 milligrams per 5 mL, give 5 mL by mouth once a day for three days. I'm staying off amoxicillin because of that possible rash. Don't pick it up today and don't start it today.
[SEG0055] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Azithromycin, once a day for three days, not the amox. When am I actually allowed to start it?

[SEG0056] person_1 (DOCTOR): If he's not better in two days, come back and start the azithromycin. Go earlier if a real fever shows up, the pain jumps, or the ear starts draining, and don't wait out the two days for those. If you're scared tonight, call the nurse line. I don't need bloodwork or a hearing test for this.

[SEG0057] person_3 (PATIENT): Can I get a sticker now, a dinosaur, because dinosaurs don't scratch? Mason's cat does, and at preschool they have goldfish crackers. One time the goldfish spilled all over the rug and everybody yelled and I still think about the crackers.
[SEG0058] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Dinosaur after the last bit, honey. Can you say the follow-up again so I don't invent a visit we don't need?

[SEG0059] person_1 (DOCTOR): Only if he needs you to come back. If he's himself again, just stay home. Most likely this is a mild ear infection we can watch, and leftover fluid from the cold is the other possibility I can't rule out. Either way I'm not starting an antibiotic in the room today.

[SEG0060] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Three nights already feels like a month, but okay, we'll wait. We'll keep the Tylenol and we won't start the other medicine unless it's the way you said. Thank you for not rushing it into his mouth.
[SEG0061] person_1 (DOCTOR): You brought him at the right time. Leo, you were brave, and the sticker box is out front.

[SEG0062] person_3 (PATIENT): I'm telling Grandma there wasn't a bug. She'll still say hot potato, she always says hot potato, even when I eat a cold popsicle. One time the popsicle was red and it dripped on the couch and she still said hot potato.
[SEG0063] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): We'll edit that story in the car. Thank you, Doctor.
[SEG0064] person_1 (DOCTOR): Anytime. If the pain suddenly gets much worse before those two days, don't sit on it.
[SEG0065] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I won't. Come on, dinosaur sticker, then home.

spec.situation: Mother and a child with ear pain and night crying after a cold; mother says no fever, grandmother says it was hot; mother unsure about the amoxicillin the child had 'long ago, got a rash maybe'; doctor decides on watchful waiting with a back-up plan.
features: self_correction: a speaker states a number, drug name or duration and then corrects it in the same turn or later ('seventy-five... no, hundred and fifty'). The label holds only the corrected value.

denial_then_admission: the patient first denies a symptom, then later describes it. The label records the symptom as present (the later, fuller answer) and does NOT also record the earlier denial as a negative finding.
doctor_misses_topics: the doctor does not ask about everything; topics never discussed are simply absent (no invented denials, no allergy line if allergies were never mentioned).
interruptions_trailing_off: people interrupt each other, trail off, or the answer comes two turns after the question.

bad.reason: Past amoxicillin use is supported, but 'discontinued' status is not stated.
Dose is wrong: transcript says 200 mg per 5 mL, give 5 mL daily; not 200 mg daily.
bad.text: azithromycin suspension (generic_name=azithromycin, dose=200 mg, route=oral, frequency=once daily, duration=3 days, indication=back-up if ear symptoms are not better, status=planned, reported_by=doctor)

bad.reason: Transcript says start if not better in two days; fever/worse pain/drainage mean go earlier, not start sooner.
bad.text: Do not start azithromycin today; start sooner if fever, sharply worse pain, or ear drainage, and call the nurse line if worried tonight (action_type=counselling, status=recommended, responsible_person=patient)
